instructions:
A principal stated a need. Regent already runs the capabilities listed (what each was built to
answer, and what it shows). For each, say whether it was built for the same need as the new one -- the same subject
and the same quantity or verdict, whatever the wording, window or how complete its answer is today -- which of the
new questions it covers (by id), and what it lacks. Regent improves a capability rather than building a duplicate,
so judge the need, not today's coverage.

new_need.sentence: How many people actually read LindyBooks these days?

questions.question: How many distinct real people have actually read LindyBooks content in the recent period?
questions.quantity: Distinct humans who engaged with LindyBooks content beyond a mere visit/open/download (e.g. read or consumed a meaningful portion, such as an engaged session or a minimum amount of content consumed), counted once per person across devices where possible
questions.population: Human readers who consumed LindyBooks content during the window
exclude: people who only landed/opened/downloaded/bought but did not read
duplicate counts of the same person across devices or sessions

questions.question: Is the number of actual readers rising, flat or falling versus prior periods ('these days')?
questions.quantity: Distinct actual readers per period compared against the previous equivalent period
questions.unit: distinct people per period, and percent change
questions.population: Same as the core reader count

questions.question: How does the number of actual readers compare with total visitors/audience (registered, subscribed or opened)?
questions.quantity: Total distinct visitors/subscribers/owners versus distinct actual readers in the same window
questions.population: All people who touched LindyBooks in the window

capabilities.answers: I want to know, at a glance, how many real people are actually using LindyBooks.
questions: How many distinct real human people actively used LindyBooks in the recent period?
What share of raw observed users or traffic was excluded as non-real, to show how reliable the real-people count is?
Is the real active user count rising or falling relative to the previous equivalent period?
metrics: Per-day rows of requests/uniques/page views, usable for trend and 7d/30d windows
HTML page views over 7 days, includes bots
HTML page views on last UTC day

same_need.description: it was built for what the new need asks (same subject, same quantity or verdict), however well it answers today

gaps: Counts 'actively used' real users, not specifically people who read content beyond a visit; no clear engaged-reading threshold
Metrics are mostly page views/uniques with bots included, so de-duplicated people across devices is uncertain
No explicit 12-month by-month series or 30d vs previous 30d percent change confirmed
No comparison of total visitors/subscribers/audience against readers (visitors_vs_readers) in same window
Windows 7d/30d/90d only partly supported (7d/30d per-day rows; 90d unclear)
